blinding_guess.why: For a second model instance, the bumper and the three cliff sensors are resolved by bare, unscoped sensor names through SensorManager::GetSensor (loads.cpp:216-220, 271), so the plugin in instance 2 can bind to the same-named sensors of instance 1; only the IMU lookup is scoped by world and model name (loads.cpp:298).

notes: All five packet elements are Gazebo sensors consumed by the model plugin GazeboRosKobuki, not ROS topics, so msg_type and definition_id are null (the code casts them to sensors::ContactSensor for bumpers, sensors::RaySensor for the three cliff sensors, sensors::ImuSensor for imu). ROS 1 package, so QoS is null. No rate is set; the sensors are read on every Gazebo world update (OnUpdate via ConnectWorldUpdateBegin, gazebo_ros_kobuki.cpp:84, 102-107). The resource names themselves (bumpers, cliff_sensor_front, cliff_sensor_left, cliff_sensor_right, imu) never appear in the snapshot: they are supplied at run time from the model SDF/URDF elements bumper_name, cliff_sensor_center_name, cliff_sensor_left_name, cliff_sensor_right_name, imu_name (the robot description comes from kobuki_description, outside the snapshot, per kobuki_gazebo/launch/includes/robot.launch.xml:7), so none of them goes into references. The front cliff resource is matched to the SDF key cliff_sensor_center_name on the strength of the error text at loads.cpp:201 and the link name cliff_sensor_front_link in kobuki_rviz_launchers/rviz/robot.rviz:80. Lookup scoping differs by element: bumper and cliff sensors use SensorManager::Instance()->GetSensor(<bare name>); the IMU uses sensors::get_sensor(<world>::<model name>::base_footprint::<imu_name>), i.e. it hard-codes the parent link base_footprint in the scoped name. Frames: no frame is declared for the consumed sensor data. The bumper contact positions/normals are treated as world coordinates (comment at updates.cpp:285, compared against model_->GetWorldPose() at updates.cpp:274); the IMU data is republished with the joint_state_ header whose frame_id is resolveTF("base_link") (updates.cpp:47-49, 146), which is the published topic's frame, not a frame of the consumed resource, so frame stays null for all ports. Units for bumper and imu are not stated in the code. The code calls SetActive(true) on every sensor (loads.cpp:246-248, 277, 304) but claims nothing exclusively, so exclusive is empty. declares/not_declared are empty because the packet lists no provided elements.
